title: Overloading vs Overriding
summary: Master the definitive comparison between method overloading and method overriding: compile-time vs runtime binding, signatures, return types, and class scopes.
learningObjectives: Master the complete 8-point comparison matrix between overloading and overriding
Identify whether a method is overloaded or overridden from code snippets

expectedOutcomes: Zero confusion between compile-time method overloading and runtime method overriding
Complete confidence answering technical interview questions on polymorphism mechanisms

activities.title: Practical Context: Distinguishing Static and Dynamic Method Variations
activities.content:
Method Overloading and Method Overriding are often confused by beginners, but they solve two entirely different engineering problems.

- **Overloading** provides multiple ways to call the same operation within a single class using different parameters (such as `save(File)` and `save(String path)`).
- **Overriding** redefines an existing operation in a subclass to provide specialized execution while keeping the exact same interface.

Distinguishing these two mechanisms is essential for designing predictable object hierarchies.

activities.title: Mastery Verification: Overloading vs Overriding (10 Questions)

questions.question: Which of the following occurs within the same class and requires different parameter lists?
options: Method Overriding
Method Overloading
Method Inlining
Method Encapsulation
questions.explanation: Method Overloading occurs within a class (or across inheritance) and requires different parameters.

questions.question: Which of the following requires an inheritance relationship and an exact matching signature?
options: Method Overloading
Method Overriding
Constructor Chaining
Static initialization
questions.explanation: Method Overriding requires a parent-child inheritance relationship and identical parameter signatures.

questions.question: Can two overloaded methods in the same class differ ONLY by their return type?
options: Yes, return type difference is sufficient for overloading
No, overloaded methods must differ in their parameter list (types, count, or order)
Only if both are declared public
Only if one returns void
questions.explanation: Return type alone cannot differentiate overloaded methods. The parameter list must differ.

questions.question: When does the Java compiler resolve which overloaded method to execute?
options: At runtime based on heap memory
At compile time based on argument types (Early/Static binding)
During garbage collection
When the JVM shuts down
questions.explanation: Method overloading is resolved at compile time based on parameter types.

questions.question: When does the JVM resolve which overridden method to execute?
options: At compile time based on reference variable type
At runtime based on the actual object in heap memory (Late/Dynamic binding)
During class loading only
Never, overridden methods cannot execute
questions.explanation: Method overriding is resolved at runtime based on the actual heap object.

questions.question: Can private methods be overloaded in the same class?
options: Yes, private methods can be overloaded freely within the same class
No, private methods cannot be overloaded
Only if they have zero parameters
Only in abstract classes
questions.explanation: Private methods can be overloaded just like any other method in the same class.

questions.question: Can private methods be overridden by a subclass?
options: Yes, if the subclass declares them public
No, private methods cannot be overridden because they are not visible to subclasses
Yes, using the @Override annotation
Only if the subclass is in the same package
questions.explanation: Private methods cannot be overridden because subclasses have no access to them.

questions.question: If Class Child extends Parent, and Parent has 'void process(int x)', while Child defines 'void process(String s)', what is this?
options: Method Overriding
Method Overloading across an inheritance hierarchy
A compilation syntax error
Method Hiding
questions.explanation: Because the parameter types differ (int vs String), Child has overloaded the inherited process method.

questions.question: Can an overriding method have a more restrictive access modifier than the parent method?
options: Yes, any access modifier is allowed
No, an overriding method cannot reduce visibility (cannot narrow access)
Only if both classes are public
Only for protected methods
questions.explanation: Overriding methods can maintain or broaden visibility, but can never narrow it.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding performance?
options: Method overriding is faster than method overloading
Method overloading has zero runtime lookup overhead because it is resolved at compile time
Both have identical runtime cost
Neither can be inlined by the JIT compiler
questions.explanation: Method overloading is resolved at compile time, eliminating runtime method lookup overhead.

interviewQA.question: What are the core differences between method overloading and method overriding in Java?
interviewQA.answer: 1. Overloading happens within the same class (or across inheritance) where methods share the same name but have different parameter lists; it is compile-time polymorphism. 2. Overriding requires two classes in an inheritance relationship where the child method has the exact same name and parameter list; it is runtime polymorphism. 3. Overloading can have different return types and access modifiers freely; overriding requires compatible (covariant) return types and cannot reduce access visibility.

interviewQA.question: Can you overload a method by changing only the return type in Java?
interviewQA.answer: No. In Java, method signature consists only of the method name and parameter types. The return type is not part of the signature used for overload resolution. If two methods in the same class have identical parameters and different return types, the compiler raises a 'method already defined' error.

interviewQA.question: Can a subclass overload a method from its superclass? Give an example.
interviewQA.answer: Yes. If class Parent defines 'void render(int quality)' and class Child extends Parent and defines 'void render(int quality, boolean antiAliased)', Child now has two overloaded render methods available: one inherited from Parent and one declared in Child.

interviewQA.question: Why can't static methods be overridden, and what happens when a subclass declares a static method with the same signature?
interviewQA.answer: Static methods are associated with the class bytecode, not with object instances in heap memory. Because polymorphism relies on runtime instance inspection, static methods cannot be dynamically dispatched. A subclass declaring a matching static method is performing Method Hiding, where call resolution depends on the compile-time reference type.

interviewQA.question: What is the difference in handling checked exceptions between overloading and overriding?
interviewQA.answer: Overloaded methods can throw any checked or unchecked exceptions independently of each other. Overriding methods are restricted: they cannot throw new or broader checked exceptions than those declared by the superclass method.

interviewQA.question: How does the JVM execute overridden methods through bytecode?
interviewQA.answer: Overridden methods are invoked using the 'invokevirtual' (or 'invokeinterface') bytecode instruction. The JVM checks the object's class header in heap memory to find its Virtual Method Table (v-table) pointer, resolving the actual method address dynamically at runtime.

practiceProblems.title: Distinguish Overloading and Overriding in a Logger
practiceProblems.description: Overload log() with different parameters, and override log() in a child class.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Combine overloading and overriding in a logging system:

1. Class Logger:
   - Method 1: public void log(String msg) printing 'LOG: <msg>'
   - Method 2 (Overload): public void log(String msg, int level) printing 'LOG [LEVEL <level>]: <msg>'

2. Class TimestampedLogger (extends Logger):
   - Method (Override): @Override public void log(String msg) printing '[2026-LOG] <msg>'

Test in Main:
Logger l1 = new Logger(); l1.log("System boot", 1);
Logger l2 = new TimestampedLogger(); l2.log("Database connection established");.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
LOG [LEVEL 1]: System boot
[2026-LOG] Database connection established
hints: Call log("System boot", 1) on Logger to test overloading.
Call log("Database connection established") on TimestampedLogger via Logger reference to test overriding.

practiceProblems.title: Shape Drawing Overload and Override
practiceProblems.description: Overload draw() by color in Shape, and override draw() in Circle from scratch.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a shape drawing hierarchy from scratch:

1. Class Shape:
   - Method 1: public void draw() printing 'Drawing generic shape'
   - Method 2 (Overload): public void draw(String color) printing 'Drawing generic shape in <color>'

2. Class Circle (extends Shape):
   - Method (Override): @Override public void draw() printing 'Drawing Circle at (0,0)'

Test in Main:
Shape s1 = new Shape(); s1.draw("Red");
Shape s2 = new Circle(); s2.draw();.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Drawing generic shape in Red
Drawing Circle at (0,0)
hints: In Shape, draw() prints generic shape, draw(color) prints generic shape in color.
